did_you_know.text: The psalm opens with joy at being invited to go up to Jerusalem and to the house of the Lord: “I rejoiced when they said to me, ‘Let us go to the house of the Lord.’”
The psalmist describes Jerusalem from the perspective of those going up to it: their feet are already standing within its gates.
Jerusalem is described as “a city joined together”—a city united and connected within itself.
The tribes go up to Jerusalem—the tribes of Israel—to bear witness to Israel’s unity and to give thanks to the name of the Lord.
Jerusalem is presented not only as a center of worship of the Lord, but also as the place where the thrones of judgment and the thrones of the house of David are located.
The verse commands people to pray for the peace of Jerusalem and links its peace with the well-being of those who love it.
The psalmist wishes peace for Jerusalem’s defenses—that is, its fortifications or security forces—and tranquility for its palaces.
The prayer for the city’s peace is offered for the sake of “my brothers and friends,” so Jerusalem’s well-being is presented as a concern for the entire community.
At the end of the psalm, the psalmist seeks good for Jerusalem for the sake of the house of the Lord our God, which stands at its center.
